Boric acid H3BO3 (B(OH)3) is monoprotic Lewis acid, accepts OH-; behaves as一元酸. Yes H3BO3 is monobasic.
Phosphorous acid H3PO3 structure HPO(OH)2: one P-H nonionizable, two OH, diprotic. So not monoprotic.
Hypophosphorous acid H3PO2 structure H2PO(OH): one OH, diprotic? Actually one ionizable H, so monoprotic.
Carbonic acid H2CO3 is diprotic.
So pairs all monoprotic: H3BO3 and H3PO2 = D. Check A has H3PO3 diprotic; B H3PO3 diprotic and H2CO3 diprotic; C H2CO3 diprotic. D yes.

Double-check: H3BO3 sometimes formula B(OH)3, accepts OH- forming [B(OH)4]- and H+, so one proton equivalent. H3PO2 has one OH, one acid proton. Good.

$H_3BO_3$（硼酸）是一元酸；$H_3PO_2$（次磷酸）也是一元酸。  
$H_3PO_3$ 是二元酸，$H_2CO_3$ 是二元酸。

因此“都是一元酸”的是：$H_3BO_3$ 和 $H_3PO_2$。

答案：D
